title: Scale drives capability
statement: Bigger networks, more data and more compute reliably buy better capability — general methods that exploit computation beat hand-engineering.
assumptions: Compute keeps getting cheaper per FLOP
Enough data exists to feed larger models
Gains show up in useful capability, not just loss

statusHistory.note: AlexNet shows large GPU-trained nets beat hand-engineered vision.
AlphaZero and Transformers reward general methods + compute.
Kaplan et al. show smooth power laws; GPT-3 confirms in May 2020.
GPT-4 extends the trend.
Pretraining returns are debated (GPT-5 reception), but scale — now in RL and inference — still drives the frontier.

outcome: Held for 2012–2026: every frontier gain came with more compute, though since 2024 the compute shifted from pretraining to RL and inference.

title: Scaling LLMs is enough for AGI
statement: Continuing to scale today's transformer LLM recipe (plus incremental unhobbling) will by itself reach human-level general intelligence.
assumptions: Next-token prediction learns a world model ('compression is understanding')
No new architectural ingredient is required

statusHistory.note: GPT-3's few-shot ability makes the 'pure scaling' bet credible to a minority.
GPT-4 strengthens the scaling camp; critics point to hallucination and reasoning failures.
Leading voices (Sutskever, Pichai) say pretraining gains are slowing; o1/o3 move gains to inference & RL.
Sutskever declares the 'age of scaling' over; Hassabis, LeCun, Sutton, Karpathy all expect extra ingredients.

outcome: Unsettled at the cutoff: capability kept rising, but via RL, search and tool use layered on LLMs — not plain scale-up — and no system meets common AGI definitions.

title: Reasoning = a new scaling axis
statement: Search, deliberation and RL at inference/post-training time ('System 2') unlock capability that pretraining alone does not.
assumptions: Verifiable rewards exist for enough domains

statusHistory.note: AlphaGo shows search + learned value functions beat pure pattern-matching in games.
Chain-of-thought prompting hints that LLMs reason better when allowed to think.
OpenAI o1 makes test-time compute a product and a scaling law.
DeepSeek-R1 replicates RL-trained reasoning in the open; reasoning goes mainstream.

outcome: Validated: reasoning models defined 2025–26 frontier progress and multiplied inference compute demand.

title: Human data runs out
statement: High-quality human text is finite; pretraining as practised will plateau and progress must come from synthetic data, RL and experience.

statusHistory.note: Chinchilla shows models were data-starved — data becomes the binding input.
Sutskever's 'peak data' talk; labs pivot to RL environments and synthetic data.
Frontier progress continues through RL/post-training; no hard wall observed, but pretraining is no longer the main lever.

outcome: Partly borne out: labs shifted to RL environments, synthetic and agentic data; no capability wall appeared.

title: LLMs are a dead end
statement: Autoregressive language models cannot reach human-level intelligence; world models, experiential RL or program synthesis are needed.
assumptions: Text lacks grounding in physical reality
A rival paradigm can be made to work at scale

statusHistory.note: Critics catalogue deep learning's limits; few alternatives are competitive.
ChatGPT's success puts LLM skeptics on the defensive.
LeCun leaves Meta to build world models; Sutskever calls for an 'age of research'; no rival paradigm has yet beaten LLM-based systems.
LLM-centric systems still define the frontier (GPT-6, Claude 5); world-model startups are funded but pre-product.

outcome: Unresolved: LLM-based systems kept improving through 2026; no alternative architecture has displaced them, but neither has scaling delivered AGI.

title: Self-supervision is the cake
statement: Most learning should come from predicting the world from raw data (self-supervised), not from labels or reward.

statusHistory.note: Supervised ImageNet-style learning dominates.
ELMo/GPT/BERT pretraining shows self-supervised text pretraining transfers.
GPT-3 makes self-supervised pretraining the foundation of the field.

outcome: Validated: self-supervised pretraining became the base layer of every foundation model.

title: RL from experience is the path
statement: Agents maximizing reward from their own experience — not imitation of human data — are the route to superhuman intelligence.
assumptions: Rich environments with reward signals can be built
Experience can be gathered cheaply enough

statusHistory.note: AlphaGo / AlphaZero: superhuman play from self-play RL.
RLHF shows RL matters for LLM usefulness.
RL with verifiable rewards drives reasoning models; continual experiential learning not yet realized.

outcome: Partly validated: RL became central to post-training and reasoning, but open-ended learning from lifelong experience is still a research goal.

title: Open weights catch the frontier
statement: Open-weight models will match or closely trail the best closed models, eroding closed-model moats.
assumptions: Open developers can access enough compute

statusHistory.note: LLaMA weights leak; open models trail GPT-4 by a wide margin.
Llama 3.1 405B reaches frontier-class on many benchmarks.
DeepSeek-R1 matches o1-class reasoning in the open at a fraction of cost.
DeepSeek V4 and Chinese open models trail the closed frontier by months; Meta retreats from fully open frontier releases.

outcome: Partly validated: open weights trail by months (Epoch estimates ~3–4), not years — but the very top remains closed and Meta itself pulled back.

title: Openness is safer than control
statement: Open release and light-touch rules protect competition and safety better than licensing regimes that favor incumbents.
assumptions: Misuse risk from open models is manageable
Regulation would be captured by incumbents

statusHistory.note: Senate hearings float licensing; open-source advocates warn of regulatory capture.
SB 1047 vetoed; EU AI Act in force with GPAI duties.
Governments restrict access to the most capable closed models (Mythos), while open Chinese models proliferate.

outcome: A values-laden debate, not settled by events: neither catastrophic open-model misuse nor regulatory capture has been clearly demonstrated by the cutoff.

title: Models commoditize
statement: Prices for a given capability collapse and model APIs become interchangeable, compressing model-layer margins.
assumptions: Efficiency gains are passed to price

statusHistory.note: GPT-4 Turbo price cuts begin a price war.
GPT-4o mini prices GPT-4-class quality ~100x below launch price.
DeepSeek prices near cost; Nvidia drops $589B in a day on efficiency fears.
Fixed-capability prices kept falling ~10x/yr, yet frontier labs reached ~$65–70B run-rates — premium frontier tiers retain pricing power.

outcome: Half right: capability-adjusted prices collapsed as predicted, but frontier model revenue exploded rather than commoditizing.

title: Cheaper AI → more total demand
statement: Falling cost per unit of intelligence increases total consumption and spending (Jevons paradox) rather than shrinking the market.
assumptions: New use cases (agents, reasoning) absorb cheap tokens

statusHistory.note: Token prices fall sharply while usage grows.
After DeepSeek, reasoning and agents multiply token demand; capex rises instead of falling.
Capex guidance reaches ~$700B+ despite collapsing unit prices.

outcome: Validated through the cutoff: unit prices fell while total compute spend and lab revenue rose steeply.

title: AI infra is a supercycle
statement: Demand for AI compute (GPUs, data centers) will sustain a multi-year, trillion-dollar build-out rather than a short boom.
assumptions: Model and agent demand keeps compounding
No efficiency shock collapses compute needs

statusHistory.note: Crypto bust hits Nvidia; AI demand still small.
Nvidia data-center revenue doubles in a quarter amid H100 shortage.
Stargate and record hyperscaler capex; DeepSeek scare does not dent spending.
Big-four capex ~$700–725B; Nvidia data-center revenue ~$89B a quarter.

outcome: Validated through Oct 2026 — the largest capex cycle in tech history — though whether it ends in overbuild is a separate, open question.

title: The capex will pay back
statement: End-user AI revenue will grow fast enough to justify the infrastructure spend; fears of an AI bubble are overdone.
assumptions: AI revenue keeps compounding at triple digits

statusHistory.note: Sequoia's $200B question: revenue far below capex.
The gap becomes 'AI's $600B question'.
Circular financing and Oracle credit spreads raise bubble fears.
Lab revenue run-rates of ~$65–70B narrow but do not close the gap with ~$700B annual capex.

outcome: Unresolved: revenue is growing faster than skeptics expected, but remains a fraction of annual capex; the payback test falls after the cutoff.

title: Power becomes the binding constraint
statement: Electricity, grid interconnects and permitted data-center shells — not chips — become the limiting factor for AI build-out.

statusHistory.note: Energy cost of training is an academic concern.
Hyperscalers sign nuclear PPAs and restart reactors.
CEOs report chips waiting on power and shells; GW-scale campuses become the unit of planning — but HBM and packaging also stay tight.
LBNL: data centers ~4.7% of US power and rising toward ~12% by 2030; power is a binding constraint alongside memory and packaging, not instead of them.

outcome: Partly validated by 2025–26: power and site readiness became a gating factor for new capacity, alongside (not instead of) chips, HBM and packaging.

title: Frontier AI consolidates
statement: Building frontier models requires capital and compute only a handful of hyperscaler-backed players can sustain.
assumptions: Efficiency shocks don't reset the race

statusHistory.note: OpenAI needs Microsoft's $1B and Azure to keep scaling.
Anthropic aligns with Amazon/Google; Microsoft deepens OpenAI tie.
Independent labs (Inflection, Character) fold into hyperscalers via license-and-hire deals.
OpenAI ($852B) and Anthropic ($965B) raise mega-rounds; 01.AI exits pretraining. DeepSeek remains the efficient exception.

outcome: Validated with an exception: the frontier narrowed to a few capital-rich US labs plus a small group of efficient Chinese labs.

title: Incumbents absorb the disruption
statement: Platform incumbents (Google, Microsoft, Meta) defend their core franchises by embedding generative AI rather than being displaced by it.

statusHistory.note: Bing Chat vows to 'make Google dance'; Google rushes Bard.
Google's Gemini 3 retakes benchmark lead; search revenue holds.
Incumbents hold distribution, but OpenAI and Anthropic became platform-scale companies in their own right.

outcome: Partly validated: no major incumbent franchise collapsed by 2026, but new AI-native platforms reached incumbent scale.

title: Value accrues to apps & agents
statement: Durable value will accrue to application, workflow and agent layers built on top of models (the software-after-Nvidia thesis).
assumptions: Workflow and data create switching costs
Apps capture a share of labor budgets

statusHistory.note: Value concentrates in Nvidia; apps are 'thin wrappers'.
Coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code) become the first breakout application category.
Model labs move up-stack into agents and apps, competing with their own customers.

outcome: Unresolved: some app-layer companies grew fast, but model labs captured much of the agent value themselves through 2026.

title: Reliable agents arrive in 2025–26
statement: Autonomous agents will join the workforce as reliable coworkers within a year or two, materially changing company output.
assumptions: Reliability over long horizons is achievable soon

statusHistory.note: Copilots launch; autonomy is aspirational.
METR shows task horizons doubling ~every 7 months; coding agents work for hours.
Enterprise pilots mostly fail to show P&L impact (MIT NANDA).
Agents are productive in coding and narrow workflows; general 'digital employees' remain unreliable.

outcome: Partly right, early elsewhere: agents transformed software engineering by 2026 but not general knowledge work.

title: Software is automated first
statement: Programming becomes the first profession transformed: natural language and neural nets increasingly write the code.

statusHistory.note: 'Software 2.0' framing; little practical automation.
GitHub Copilot preview shows LLM code completion works.
Agentic coding (Claude Code, Cursor) becomes the killer app.
AI writes the majority of code at leading labs and many startups; coding agents drive lab revenue.

outcome: Validated: software development was the first large-scale professional domain transformed by AI.

title: Human-level AGI is near
statement: Human-level (or greater) general AI will arrive within a few years of the claim — on most such claims, before ~2030.

statusHistory.note: AGI timelines are speculative; most researchers say decades.
GPT-4 shortens many experts' timelines (Hinton, Bengio).
Deadlines set for 2025 (e.g. Musk) pass without AGI; Amodei/Aschenbrenner windows (2026–27) still open.

outcome: Unresolved: no consensus AGI by the cutoff; several specific near-term deadlines (2025) were missed while capability rose quickly.

title: Advanced AI is an existential risk
statement: Advanced AI could cause catastrophic or existential harm and warrants strong safety work and governance now.
assumptions: Alignment is not solved by default

statusHistory.note: Bostrom's Superintelligence frames the risk; most researchers dismiss it.
CAIS statement signed by Hinton, Bengio, Altman, Amodei, Hassabis; LeCun dissents.
Governments restrict frontier cyber-capable models (Glasswing/Mythos); evaluations show deceptive behaviors; no catastrophe observed.

outcome: Not resolvable by observation at the cutoff; the risk debate moved from fringe to government policy.

title: AI causes mass job loss
statement: AI will displace a large share of human jobs (or tasks) within roughly a decade of the claim.

statusHistory.note: Radiology and driving cited as first to go.
Five-year radiology deadline passes; radiologist demand still rises — first concrete miss for the thesis.
Early evidence of reduced entry-level hiring in AI-exposed occupations; no aggregate unemployment spike.
Aggregate employment intact at the cutoff; most decade-scale deadlines not yet reached.

outcome: Unresolved overall; specific early calls (radiologists by 2021, 80% of doctors' work by 2025) failed, while entry-level effects are emerging.

title: China reaches near-parity
statement: Chinese AI will match or nearly match the US frontier despite compute disadvantages and export controls.

statusHistory.note: China's AI plan targets leadership by 2030.
US export controls aim to freeze China's compute.
DeepSeek-R1 shocks markets with near-frontier reasoning.
DeepSeek V4 / Qwen / Kimi trail the frontier by months; compute still constrains China.

outcome: Partly validated: China reached near-parity in open models with months of lag, not leadership; compute access remains its binding constraint.

title: AI becomes an engine of science
statement: AI systems will solve fundamental scientific problems and become primary tools of discovery.

statusHistory.note: AlphaGo hints at superhuman search in hard domains.
AlphaFold 2 solves protein structure prediction at CASP14.
Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold.
Models contribute novel math results; AI-designed drugs still in early trials.

outcome: Validated for structural biology and parts of mathematics; broader 'AI scientist' claims remain partial.

title: Language becomes the interface
statement: Natural-language conversation becomes a primary computing interface — 'English is the new programming language'.

statusHistory.note: Chatbots ('bots are the new apps') underwhelm.
ChatGPT reaches 100M users in two months.
Coding by natural language ('vibe coding') goes mainstream.

outcome: Validated: conversational interfaces reached hundreds of millions of weekly users and natural language became a programming interface.

title: Full self-driving is a year away
statement: Camera-only neural driving will deliver unsupervised autonomy at scale within about a year of each claim.
assumptions: Fleet data solves the long tail

statusHistory.note: The promised 2017 coast-to-coast autonomous drive does not happen.
No million robotaxis in 2020.
Robotaxi coverage of half the US by end-2025 does not happen; service remains limited.

outcome: Falsified on the stated timelines (2017, 2020, 2025); whether vision-only autonomy ultimately scales is a separate, open question.

title: Skill ≠ intelligence
statement: Benchmark skill can be bought with data; intelligence is efficiency of adapting to novelty, and AI capability is 'jagged'.

statusHistory.note: ARC benchmark introduced; LLMs score near zero.
o3 breaks ARC-AGI-1 with heavy test-time compute.
ARC-AGI-2 again exposes a large human–AI gap; 'jagged intelligence' becomes common vocabulary — though scores rose quickly later in 2025.

outcome: Partly validated as a measurement critique: frontier systems remain jagged, but each new benchmark gap narrowed faster than the critique implied.

title: Enterprise AI pays off fast
statement: Generative AI will quickly deliver large, measurable enterprise productivity gains and ROI.

statusHistory.note: Copilot priced at $30/user/month; ROI unproven.
MIT NANDA: ~95% of GenAI pilots show no P&L impact; coding is the exception.
Enterprise spend surges (lab run-rates), concentrated in coding and customer operations; economy-wide productivity gains not yet visible in statistics.

outcome: Partial: spending and adoption are real and concentrated; macro productivity effects had not appeared by the cutoff.
